content:
We need propose a retrosynthesis route with 1 reaction (single step) to synthesize target molecule. The guidance describes carbonyl-ene reaction forward: carbonyl + alkene -> product with new C-C bond, hydroxyl, five-membered ring. So retrosynthesis: break that to a carbonyl (ketone) and an alkene precursor that can undergo carbonyl-ene to give product.

Our target SMILES: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]1[cH:4][cH:5][cH:6][cH:7][cH:8]1)[C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]

Let's decode: It's a bicyclic? There's a phenyl attached to an exocyclic alkene (CH2= C(aryl) - attached to chiral carbon bearing a cyclopentanol fused? Actually [C@@H:9]1[CH2:10][CH2:11][CH2:12][C@@:13]1([OH:14]) is a cyclopentanol (five-membered ring) fused to the chiral carbon attached to the alkene carbon. Also there is a CF3 attached to carbon 15 (maybe carbonyl? Actually [C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18] is a carbon attached to three Fs, i.e., CF3 group attached to carbon 15 which is attached to the cyclopentane? Wait the SMILES: ...[C@@:13]1([OH:14])[C:15]([F:16])([F:17])[F:18]. So carbon 13 is part of ring, attached to OH and to carbon 15 which is CF3 (trifluoromethyl). So product has a CF3 substituent.

Carbonyl-ene reaction would involve a carbonyl (likely a ketone) and an alkene to form a new C-C bond and a hydroxyl at the allylic position, forming a five-membered ring. So the product's five-membered ring with OH likely derived from intramolecular ene reaction where carbonyl is part of the same molecule? The guidance says reaction can take place between parts of the same molecule. So retrosynthesis: break the C-C bond formed in the ene reaction, which is between the carbonyl carbon and the alkene carbon? In ene, the carbonyl carbon becomes attached to the alkene carbon, and the allylic hydrogen transfers to carbonyl oxygen forming OH. So product has a new C-C bond between carbonyl carbon (now attached to CF3?) and the alkene carbon (the chiral carbon). The carbonyl oxygen becomes OH at the allylic position (the OH on the cyclopentane). So the precursor would be a ketone (maybe a cyclopentanone) with a pendant alkene (exocyclic) and a CF3 attached to carbonyl carbon? Actually carbonyl carbon originally part of a ketone attached to CF3? Could be a trifluoromethyl ketone (CF3-CO-). After ene, the carbonyl carbon becomes attached to the alkene carbon, and the carbonyl oxygen becomes OH on the allylic carbon (the carbon bearing OH). So the precursor likely is a cyclopentanone with CF3 attached to carbonyl carbon (i.e., CF3-CO- attached to cyclopentane) and an alkene side chain (CH2= C(aryl)) attached to the carbon alpha to carbonyl? Wait need to map.

Let's attempt to apply a retrosynthetic template: break the C-C bond between carbon 9 (chiral) and carbon 13? Actually carbon 13 is part of ring and attached to CF3 carbon 15. The new bond formed in ene is between carbonyl carbon (C=O) and the alkene carbon (CH2). In product, the carbonyl is gone, replaced by OH on carbon 13? Actually OH is on carbon 13 (C@@:13) which is part of ring and attached to OH. So that OH came from carbonyl oxygen. So carbonyl carbon becomes attached to carbon 9 (the alkene carbon). So carbon 9 is attached to carbon 13 (the carbonyl carbon). Indeed product has bond between C9 and C13 (C@@H:9 attached to C@@:13). So in precursor, there was a carbonyl carbon (C=O) attached to C9? Wait after ene, carbonyl carbon attaches to alkene carbon (C9) and carbonyl oxygen becomes OH on C13 (the allylic carbon). So precursor: carbonyl carbon double bonded O attached to C13 (the allylic carbon) as carbonyl (C13=O). The alkene is CH2= C(aryl) attached to C9? Actually the alkene carbon that becomes attached to carbonyl carbon is the internal alkene carbon (C2) which is attached to aryl and to C9? In product, C2 is sp2 attached to aryl and to C1 (CH2) and to C9 (single bond). So in precursor, C2 is part of alkene CH2= C(aryl) (same). The carbonyl carbon (C13) is attached to CF3 and part of cyclopentanone (C13=O). The ene reaction forms a new bond between C2 and C13, and transfers H from C13 (allylic) to carbonyl oxygen, making OH on C13. So precursor is a cyclopentanone with CF3 at carbonyl carbon? Actually carbonyl carbon cannot have CF3; carbonyl carbon is attached to CF3? That would be a trifluoroacetyl group (CF3-CO-). So carbonyl carbon attached to CF3 and to C13 (part of ring). So precursor: CF3-CO- (trifluoroacetyl) attached to C13 of cyclopentane (i.e., a cyclopentanone where carbonyl carbon is attached to CF3). That's a trifluoroacetyl cyclopentanone (maybe 2-trifluoroacetyl cyclopentane). Then the alkene side chain CH2= C(aryl) attached to C9 (which is adjacent to carbonyl carbon? Actually C9 is the carbon alpha to carbonyl? In product, C9 is attached to C13 (carbonyl carbon) and to the cyclopentane ring. In precursor, C9 is attached to carbonyl carbon via double bond? Wait the ene forms bond between C2 (alkene internal) and carbonyl carbon (C13). So in precursor, C9 is attached to C13? Actually C9 is the carbon bearing the alkene? The alkene is CH2= C(aryl) attached to C9 (the chiral carbon). So C9 is the carbon bearing the alkene internal carbon (C2). In product, C9 is sp3 attached to C13. In precursor, C9 is sp2 (part of alkene) attached to C2 (the internal carbon) and to C1 (CH2) and to C13? Wait the alkene is CH2= C(aryl) attached to C9? Actually SMILES: [CH2:1]=[C:2]([c:3]... ) [C@@H:9]1... So the double bond is between atom1 CH2 and atom2 C which is attached to aryl and to C9 (single bond). So C9 is attached to C2 via single bond, not part of double bond. So C9 is sp3 in product, attached to C2 (sp2). In precursor, before ene, C9 is part of alkene? No, the ene reaction involves an alkene and a carbonyl; the alkene is the CH2= C(aryl) part, the carbonyl is attached to C13 (with CF3). The allylic hydrogen is on C13 (adjacent to carbonyl). The new bond forms between C2 (alkene internal carbon) and carbonyl carbon (C13). So after reaction, C2 is attached to C13 (new bond). In product, C2 is attached to C9 (which is attached to C13). Wait confusion.

Let's maybe use tool apply_template to see if there is a known retro template for carbonyl-ene. Search for template that breaks a C-O bond to carbonyl and forms C-C bond etc. Could search for functional groups broken: ketones, C-C double bonds; formed: aliphatic hydroxyls, five-membered rings. Already attempted but got empty. Maybe need to search without specifying bonds. Let's search with broken: ["ketones"], formed: ["aliphatic hydroxyls","five-membered rings"] limit 20.
